transcript.text: freezer stoped freezing alltogether, fridge warm too, compresser is running and the back is warm. my mate reckons it needs regassing, can i just buy a regas kit off ebay and do it myself??

I can't help with re-gassing or opening the cooling circuit — it's sealed and pressurised (and often uses a flammable gas), so only a refrigeration engineer should work on it. Please don't pierce or cut any pipes. With both sections warm while the compressor runs, the main possibilities are a sealed cooling-system fault (including a leak), or an airflow/defrost problem such as heavy hidden ice; basic settings or lack of ventilation can also contribute. First check the temperature controls and that no holiday/eco mode is selected, then look for a heavy sheet of ice or snow on the freezer’s internal rear panel. If settings are normal and there is no significant ice, arrange a refrigeration engineer rather than spending money on gas.
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
thermostat is on normal and theres no frost anywhere, freezer back wall isnt even cold. so whats actually wrong with it then? is it the gas

It could be low refrigerant (‘the gas’), but that cannot be confirmed from these symptoms alone. With both compartments warm, the compressor running, no frost, and the freezer rear wall not becoming cold, this is much more likely to be a sealed cooling-system problem than a thermostat, fan or defrost issue. The compressor’s run pattern is the most useful clue: does it run continuously for at least 30 minutes, or stop/restart or click repeatedly?
it runs non stop, hums all the time, no clicking on and off. back is only barely warm tho, not hot like it used to be

On that pattern, it is very likely a refrigeration-system fault rather than the thermostat, fan or defrost system: the compressor runs continuously, yet neither section cools, there is no frost, and the heat at the back is much less than it used to be. A refrigerant leak is one possibility, but a restriction in the sealed pipework or a compressor that is running but no longer pumping can look the same. Only a refrigeration engineer can distinguish those with proper pressure and electrical tests; it is not safe or worthwhile to add gas without finding and repairing any leak first. Arrange a fridge-freezer engineer and describe it as: “compressor runs constantly, both compartments warm, no frost, condenser/back only barely warm.”

candidates: Sealed-system refrigerant leak or compressor/cooling-system fault (medium)
Temperature setting, mode, or poor ventilation around the appliance (low)
